skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Create Conventional Commit messages, inspect diffs, stage selected files, and run git commit with local Git commands when the user requests a commit.
skill.summary: Helps create focused Conventional Commits from local repository changes.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline commit type examples, and a secret-warning sentence. The skill still includes Bash-based Git staging and commit workflows, so the git add and git commit command patterns remain confirmed external-command risks. I found no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Git staging examples can include unintended files.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit file list from git status before staging, and avoid broad wildcard staging unless the user confirms it.

remediation.issue: The multi-line commit example uses shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer git commit -F with a temporary message file, or pass safely quoted message arguments without shell command substitution.

remediation.issue: Secret handling is only documented as a warning.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory review step for .env files, credential files, and private keys before running git add or git commit.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages and staging the right files can slow reviews. This skill inspects local changes and creates focused Conventional Commits.
actual_capabilities: Checks staged and unstaged changes with git diff and git status.
Selects a Conventional Commit type from the documented commit type list.
Suggests a scope and short imperative description from the diff.
Stages specific files, patterns, or hunks when a commit needs grouping.
Runs single-line or multi-line git commit commands for approved changes.
Applies safety rules for hooks, destructive commands, and protected branches.
limitations: Requires a local Git repository and Bash access.
Cannot guarantee that generated messages satisfy every project policy.
May need user review when diffs contain unrelated changes.
Does not replace secret scanning or repository compliance checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Commits
use_cases.description: Group related local changes and create a clear commit before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team History
use_cases.description: Use Conventional Commit types so changelogs and release tools receive consistent messages.

use_cases.title: Commit Maintenance Work
use_cases.description: Capture dependency, test, documentation, or cleanup changes with the correct commit type.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Current Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a normal commit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Conventional Commit for my current changes. Show the files you plan to include before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Selected Files
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants one logical commit from a larger working tree.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the diff and commit only the changes related to the authentication fix. Leave unrelated files unstaged.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Type And Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: User already knows the desired Conventional Commit metadata.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit with type fix and scope api. Generate the description from the staged diff.

prompt_templates.title: Create Breaking Change Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced commit that needs a body and footer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the staged diff and create a Conventional Commit with a breaking change footer. Include a concise body explaining the migration impact.

output_examples.input: Commit the staged bug fix for token refresh handling.
output_examples.output: The skill would inspect the staged diff, choose the fix type, and create a message like fix(auth): refresh expired tokens.

output_examples.input: Commit documentation updates and reference issue 456.
output_examples.output: The skill would stage the documentation files, choose the docs type, and include Refs #456 in the commit message.

output_examples.input: Create a breaking change commit for the config loader update.
output_examples.output: The skill would create a commit with a breaking-change marker and a footer describing the changed config behavior.

best_practices: Review the staged file list before any commit is created.
Keep each commit focused on one logical change.
Use explicit file paths when staging sensitive or mixed working trees.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad wildcards when the working tree contains unrelated files.
Do not commit secrets, credential files, or private keys.
Do not skip hooks or change Git configuration unless the user explicitly asks.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It can run git commit when the user requests a commit and the repository state is ready.

faq.question: Does it follow Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects a type, optional scope, short description, and optional body or footer.

faq.question: Can it stage only some files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can stage explicit files, patterns, or hunks for one logical commit.

faq.question: Will it force push or reset my branch?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs agents to avoid destructive Git commands unless the user explicitly requests them.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets before committing?
faq.answer: It warns against committing secrets, but it does not replace a dedicated secret scanner.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
